title: Track OpenClaw releases: compatibility range and update smoke
description: Decision: track OpenClaw releases rather than chase version agnosticism. The feature-plugin and Control UI APIs are experimental, so no plugin can be fully agnostic; the practical guarantee is a smoke script run after every openclaw update on the operator's host, then bump build.openclawVersion and the tested range and push. Smoke installs the plugin into an isolated Gateway on the installed build and checks load, contract validation, page registration, a family.week query, the service scheduler, and the SQLite store. README states the tested OpenClaw version.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke script passes on 2026.9.7 against an isolated Gateway and fails with a named step when any integration point breaks.
notes:
DONE in 006a74e + 7 fix commits through 6abc658. Allowlist change for scripts/ is 99316c2; the Step 0 docs sync is e001a41.

Ships: scripts/smoke.ts (npm run smoke), tsconfig.scripts.json, typecheck:scripts added to npm run check, openclaw.install.minHostVersion '>=2026.9.7', README and AGENTS.md state the tested version and the smoke. package-lock.json deliberately left untracked for s5k.31.5.

Steps, each failing with its own name: host version, plugin load, manifest, contract validation, family.week query, page registration, service scheduler, sqlite store, host json limits, update path. Isolation per AGENTS.md: temp state dir, loopback bind, free port that is never 18789, logging.file inside the temp dir, state removed on exit. OCFP_SMOKE_KEEP=1 keeps it, OCFP_SMOKE_HOST_BIN chooses the host.

Verified: normal run passes end to end in ~40s with exit 0 and no leftover state; host exiting non-zero, a non-executable path, a spawn failure, a SIGTERM-deaf host, a host leaking a background child, an interrupt during a host call, an interrupt during readiness, and a missing host binary each produce exactly one named 'smoke: <step> failed:' line, no stack trace, no surviving descendant and no leaked state.

Environment findings, not plugin defects:
1. Two builds of the same OpenClaw version disagree on the Control UI bundle hash (the bundles are semantically identical, differing only in minifier identifier names). dist/ therefore satisfies 'plugins build --check' for exactly one build. dist/ is left on the pinned build per the pin-and-test rule; the smoke's manifest step fails by name against the other and says to rebuild with it.
2. On pinned 2026.9.7 (c074824), installing this repo fails with 'conflicting child rows' when our own node_modules holds a real openclaw directory: the host walks the install path, discovers its 64 bundled extensions under node_modules/openclaw/dist/extensions, and counts them as children of our install record. A git install is unaffected because openclaw is linked, not copied. The smoke installs from a clean staged copy to avoid it.

Known limitations, all documented in AGENTS.md: the scheduler step is a host liveness probe; the store step only checks the state dir is writable and that no file naming this plugin leaked outside it; the update step cannot exercise a git refresh because the smoke installs from a local copy.

Accepted residual risks, not fixed: killGroup's ref'd SIGKILL poll could in principle signal a recycled pid within its 2s window, and it resolves on a tick so a clean run pays about 2s after its last line. Neither affects the pass/fail contract.

Review history: seven rounds. Each round found a real defect, and several commit messages in this bead overclaimed what had been verified.
close_reason: Done in 006a74e through 6abc658 (allowlist 99316c2). npm run smoke runs 10 named steps against an isolated Gateway on the host under test; full check set green; failure paths verified to report one named step with no stack trace, no orphans and no leftover state.

title: Approvals for risky writes and kid requests via OpenClaw plugin approvals
description: Operator decision: use OpenClaw's native plugin approvals only; no custom draft store. A before_tool_call hook on the family write tools returns requireApproval for deletes, moves to another calendar, recurring series edits (scope future/all), and permission-table needs-approval results (kid -> someone else's calendar). Title <= 80 chars naming the action and event, description <= 512 naming who asked, which calendar, and when; allowedDecisions ['allow-once','deny']; timeoutMs 600000 (the 10-minute maximum). Deny, timeout, or no connected approver blocks the write; the tool result tells the requester plainly and suggests asking again when a parent is around. Approvers are people whose role has operator.approvals. Plain creates by an allowed requester write immediately with undo. The write log records approved/denied/timed-out outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: A kid on Discord asks to add to a parent's calendar: approvals.plugin delivers the request to a parent's Discord DM; allow commits exactly once; deny or the 10-minute timeout leaves Google untouched and the kid gets a clear reply. A delete from Discord chat requires the same DM approval. A Control UI chat approval is not the proof, because that approval is bound to the requesting device.
notes:
Multiplayer finding: OpenClaw already has plugin approvals. A before_tool_call hook returning requireApproval {title<=80, description<=512, severity, allowedDecisions, timeoutMs<=600000, scope} creates a plugin: approval delivered to every approval surface (Control UI approval page, browser/macOS push notifications, chat forwarding) and fails closed on deny/timeout/no route (docs/plugins/plugin-permission-requests.md). Approvers are people whose role has operator.approvals (parents), so kids cannot approve their own requests. Candidate design: use it for risky writes and kid requests instead of a custom draft UI; the write log records the outcome. Limit: 10-minute max wait, so a request a parent does not see in time is denied and must be re-asked, unless long-lived drafts are kept for that case.
Prereq review 2026-09-30, operator decision: kids write only through Discord/the agent; page writes are parent-only. Reason: before_tool_call requireApproval fires only for agent tool calls (page session actions and commands are not tool-wrapped), and approvals raised from a Control UI chat are bound to the requesting device, so a parent needs operator.admin to resolve them. Discord-originated approvals route to parents via approvals.plugin (mode targets = parents' Discord DMs); with no route the call fails closed. requireApproval has no approver field (shipped hook types), so parent targeting is config, not plugin code.

title: Role-to-calendar write permissions
description: Build the role-to-calendar permission table before any write handler exists. There is no write handler today, so nothing can write to a calendar yet. Identity is resolved once at the boundary: Discord tool calls match requesterSenderId to the roster discordId; page session-actions require operator.write (the kid role lacks it, so page writes are parent-level); Control UI chat with no resolvable identity uses a configured unknownRequesterRole (default kid). Handlers never branch on role directly; they ask the table.

title: Prerequisite: multi-user Gateway for the family
description: Per-person Control UI access follows the household access mode in s5k.32.3. LAN mode: Caddy basic_auth, one bcrypt user per member, header_up X-Forwarded-User, Gateway auth.mode trusted-proxy, trustedProxies [127.0.0.1] with allowLoopback only when Caddy is the sole local listener, allowUsers = those usernames. Internet mode: Tailscale Serve or Cloudflare Access. Token or password auth shares the single Owner profile, and users.self fails with 'requires an authenticated user', so per-person page identity starts at this cutover. Kid role: operator.read and operator.sessions.write, no operator.write. Parent role adds operator.write. Assign with users.setRole. Discord identity stays the roster discordId matched to requesterSenderId. Changing auth or ingress on the live Gateway needs operator approval.
notes:
Investigation (docs/start/teams.md, docs/gateway/team-server.md, docs/gateway/tailscale.md, docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md, docs/concepts/user-model.md): multi-user is the same Control UI reached through an identity-bearing URL, not a separate client. Paired devices with token/password auth all share the one Owner profile. Per-person profiles come only from Tailscale Serve (gateway.tailscale.mode serve + gateway.auth.allowTailscale), a trusted proxy (Pomerium, Caddy+OAuth, nginx+oauth2-proxy, Authelia-style forward auth; auth.mode trusted-proxy, token removed), or Cloudflare Access + Tunnel. Profiles are created on first verified sign-in; admin assigns roles with users.setRole; gateway.roles defines per-role agents, sessions.others, scopes, sandbox. All three give HTTPS, which native plugin pages also need. A Gateway on token auth with a LAN bind and no proxy has no HTTPS path, so LAN-paired browsers cannot load native plugin pages. Changing auth/ingress on the live Gateway needs operator approval.

title: Plugin SQLite store in a worker thread
description: Non-bundled plugins are refused openKeyedStore/openBlobStore, and plugin-sdk sqlite-runtime/sqlite-worker-runtime are private-local. Own one file at <stateDir>/plugins/oc-family-pack/oc-family-pack.sqlite (dir 0700, file 0600). node:sqlite DatabaseSync owned by a worker_threads worker (never the Gateway main thread), WAL + busy timeout, STRICT tables, an oc_family_pack_schema_migrations table (pattern: openclaw extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-schema.ts). Synchronous write transactions inside the worker; reread rows before compare-and-set. Small repository interface (reminder ledger, prefs, email signals, later chores). If upstreamed as bundled: keep path and schema, swap plumbing to openSqliteWorkerStore.
design:
# s5k.19 design: plugin-owned SQLite store in a worker thread

Proven on an isolated 2026.9.7 Gateway (proof logs: docs/research/storage/).
Uses only public contracts: service ctx.stateDir, api.registerService, node:worker_threads,
node:sqlite, manifest backupResources. No openclaw sqlite/plugin-state/process-runtime subpaths
(private-local; keyed/blob stores throw PluginTrustRefusalError for non-bundled plugins,
openclaw src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts:202-218).

## Location and files
- Path: join(ctx.stateDir, "plugins", "oc-family-pack", "oc-family-pack.sqlite") from the
  service start context (typed stateDir; host passes STATE_DIR, src/plugins/services.ts:557).
  Observed equal to api.runtime.state.resolveStateDir(). Same layout as bundled workboard and
  team-reports (<state>/plugins/<id>/<id>.sqlite).
- Worker creates dir 0700 and file 0600 before open; chmods -wal/-shm 0600 after WAL is on.
- Worker entry: new URL("./store-worker.js", import.meta.url) in dist/store.js. The host runs
  a captured copy of the package (<state>/tmp/plugin-captures/.../dist/); the sibling worker
  file travels with it (observed workerFileExists=true). Do not use api.runtimeSource: it points
  at the install dir (<state>/git/git-*/repo/dist/index.js), which update replaces.
- Built by the existing `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` (dist/store-worker.js). The worker imports
  no openclaw modules. Only dist/store-worker.js imports node:sqlite (static check in CI:
  grep -l node:sqlite dist/*.js must equal dist/store-worker.js).
- `openclaw plugins pack` artifacts are not supported once the store lands (pack rejects
  import.meta and multi-file backends, docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md:310-319). git/npm
  installs are unaffected (observed).

## Connection
PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000; journal_mode=WAL (assert result 'wal'); synchronous=NORMAL;
foreign_keys=ON. Mirrors workboard (extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-schema.ts:10-12,336-343).
Host guarantees a WAL-safe SQLite and Node >=24.16 (docs/install/node-compatibility.md:15-21,42-44);
observed SQLite 3.53.0. Set package.json engines.node to ">=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0".

## Tables (STRICT; one named consumer each)
```sql
CREATE TABLE oc_family_pack_schema_migrations (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,               -- 'NNNN-slug'
  applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT;

-- s5k.34.2 write log + idempotency, s5k.34.3 drafts, s5k.34.4 undo
CREATE TABLE write_log (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,              -- request key hash (requester+op+fields+turn id)
  requester TEXT NOT NULL,           -- roster profileId
  op TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (op IN ('create','update','move','delete','revert')),
  calendar_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_calendar_id TEXT,           -- move destination
  event_id TEXT,                     -- null until gog returns it
  before_json TEXT,                  -- null for create
  after_json TEXT,                   -- null for delete
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('awaiting-approval','intent','committed','failed','denied','timed-out','reverted')),
  approver TEXT,
  reverts_key TEXT,                  -- no FK so age pruning never blocks
  error TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (op <> 'move' OR target_calendar_id IS NOT NULL),
  CHECK (op <> 'revert' OR reverts_key IS NOT NULL)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX write_log_requester_idx ON write_log(requester, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX write_log_event_idx ON write_log(calendar_id, event_id, created_at DESC);

-- s5k.11 reminders: one row per (event version, lead, owner)
CREATE TABLE reminder_ledger (
  calendar_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  event_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  event_updated TEXT NOT NULL,       -- gog 'updated' of the event version
  lead_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lead_minutes >= 0),
  member_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('claimed','held','sent','skipped')),
  due_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  release_at INTEGER,                -- quiet-hours window end
  settled_at INTEGER,
  CHECK (status <> 'held' OR release_at IS NOT NULL),
  PRIMARY KEY (calendar_id, event_id, event_updated, lead_minutes, member_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX reminder_ledger_held_idx ON reminder_ledger(release_at) WHERE status = 'held';
CREATE INDEX reminder_ledger_due_idx ON reminder_ledger(due_at);

-- s5k.35.1 delivery receipts + once-per-streak admin alert
CREATE TABLE delivery_log (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  delivery_key TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'brief:daily:2026-10-01', 'reminder:<ledger key>'
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('brief','reminder','admin-alert')),
  target TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'member:<profileId>' or 'channel:<config key>', never raw Discord ids
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sent','failed')),
  error TEXT,
  admin_alerted_at INTEGER,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (status = 'failed' OR (error IS NULL AND admin_alerted_at IS NULL))
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX delivery_log_kind_idx ON delivery_log(kind, at DESC);

-- s5k.33.1 change poll cursor + stale age + backoff
CREATE TABLE calendar_cursors (
  calendar_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  cursor TEXT,                       -- last seen 'updated' watermark for gog calendar changed
  last_success_at INTEGER,
  last_error TEXT,
  last_error_at INTEGER,
  consecutive_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (consecutive_failures >= 0)
) STRICT;

-- s5k.11 chat-toggled reminder mode; config holds the default, this row overrides it
CREATE TABLE member_prefs (
  member_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  reminder_mode TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reminder_mode IN ('dm','channel','off')),
  updated_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT;
```
Deferred until their beads activate (additive migrations): email signals (s5k.23), chores (s5k.14).

write_log state machine (enforced by writeLog.transition, CAS on `from`):
awaiting-approval -> intent | denied | timed-out (native plugin approval outcome, <= 10 min, held in the host, not here); intent -> committed | failed; failed -> intent (retry same key); committed -> reverted (undo).
begin inserts 'intent' (direct write) or 'awaiting-approval' (a native approval is open) before gog runs, so a
crash between gog success and the commit leaves an 'intent' row that the retry resolves by the
gog private-prop lookup (s5k.34.2). Undo = latest committed row by requester inside the window
with op <> 'revert' and no row whose reverts_key = its key; the revert is a new row.

## Migrations
- Ordered array compiled into the worker: [{ id: "0001-initial", sql }, ...].
- On worker start: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oc_family_pack_schema_migrations; then for each
  migration, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, re-check the id inside the transaction, exec, insert id, COMMIT.
  Safe if two workers overlap during a plugin reload (observed: config reload restarts service).
- Between releases only additive changes (new table, nullable column, index). A rebuild needs a
  new migration that creates, copies, and swaps in one transaction.
- Applied ids unknown to this build (plugin downgrade) are reported in `ready.unknown`, logged
  as a warning, and the store keeps serving (observed run6).
- No PRAGMA user_version; the migrations table is the single version record.

## Worker protocol
```ts
type WriteStatus = "awaiting-approval" | "intent" | "committed" | "failed" | "denied" | "timed-out" | "reverted";
type StoreOps = {
  "writeLog.begin":        { req: { key; requester; op; calendarId; targetCalendarId?; beforeJson?; afterJson?; awaitingApproval?: boolean; now }; res: { row: WriteLogRow; inserted: boolean } };
  "writeLog.transition":   { req: { key; from: WriteStatus[]; to: WriteStatus; eventId?; afterJson?; approver?; error?; now }; res: { row: WriteLogRow } | { conflict: WriteLogRow } };
  "writeLog.lastUndoable": { req: { requester; since: number }; res: WriteLogRow | null };
  "writeLog.history":      { req: { calendarId; eventId; limit: number }; res: WriteLogRow[] };
  "reminder.claim":        { req: { key: ReminderKey; dueAt; holdUntil?: number }; res: { claimed: boolean; status } };
  "reminder.settle":       { req: { key: ReminderKey; status: "sent" | "skipped"; now }; res: void };
  "reminder.releaseHeld":  { req: { now }; res: ReminderKey[] };
  "delivery.record":       { req: { deliveryKey; kind; target; status: "sent" | "failed"; error?; now }; res: { alertAdmin: boolean } };
  "delivery.latest":       { req: { kind }; res: { sent?: DeliveryRow; failed?: DeliveryRow } };
  "cursor.get":            { req: { calendarId }; res: CursorRow | null };
  "cursor.recordSuccess":  { req: { calendarId; cursor; now }; res: void };
  "cursor.recordFailure":  { req: { calendarId; error; now }; res: { consecutiveFailures: number } };
  "prefs.list":            { req: {}; res: MemberPrefRow[] };
  "prefs.set":             { req: { memberId; reminderMode; updatedBy; now }; res: void };
  "maintenance.prune":     { req: { now; calendarIds: string[]; memberIds: string[] }; res: Record<string, number> };
};
// main -> worker: { id: number; op: K; input: StoreOps[K]["req"] } | { type: "close" }
// worker -> main: { type: "ready"; appliedNow; applied; unknown; sqliteVersion; journalMode }
//               | { type: "result"; id; ok: true; result } | { type: "result"; id; ok: false; error }
//               | { type: "closed" }
```
The worker holds one handler per op in a typed record (no switch). Every write handler runs in
one synchronous BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and rereads the row before compare-and-set; no
Promise or await inside. alertAdmin is decided inside the same transaction (failed, and no
failed row for the same kind+target with admin_alerted_at since the last sent row).

## Main thread
- Service "family-store" (registered in setup via api.registerService, feature-plugin.d.ts:34)
  with reload.configPrefixes ["plugins.entries.oc-family-pack.config"].
- start: spawn worker, await `ready` (migrations done), run maintenance.prune with the parsed
  roster, start a 24 h prune timer.
- call<K>(op, input): Promise<res>: id -> resolver map; one postMessage per call.
- Feature handlers read the store through the service closure; before ready or after failure
  they fail with "Family store is not ready; check the Gateway log for oc-family-pack".
- Worker error/exit: reject every pending call, ctx.serviceHealth.reportFailure(error), reopen
  lazily on the next call (single flight; open is convergent).
- stop: post close (worker runs wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE), closes, exits); terminate() after 5 s.
- Main thread never imports node:sqlite.

## Retention (maintenance.prune, one transaction per table)
- write_log: rows older than 90 days deleted (all statuses); no expiry sweep (approvals time out in the host)
  every minute.
- reminder_ledger: due_at older than 14 days deleted.
- delivery_log: older than 30 days deleted, keeping the newest row per kind (page shows last brief).
- calendar_cursors / member_prefs: rows whose calendar/member is no longer in config deleted at
  service start (config is the roster owner; config changes restart the service).

## Backup, update, uninstall
- Manifest: "backupResources": [{ "disposition": "include", "scope": "state",
  "relativePath": "plugins/oc-family-pack" }]. Applies to any activated, loadable plugin, no
  origin gate (openclaw src/plugins/manifest-backup-resources.ts:109-127). Gives verified online
  snapshots with committed WAL and no sidecars (docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md:292-311).
  Observed: offline and online backups verify with no warnings; an undeclared plugin SQLite file
  gets the "archived as opaque bytes" warning. `openclaw plugins build` keeps the field.
- Host `openclaw update`: the DB sits outside host-owned paths; host migrations never open it.
  Plugin reinstall (--force) and `plugins update` keep it (observed rows 3 and 4).
- Uninstall: removes plugin config, install record, and <state>/git/... install dir; leaves
  `{"enabled": false}` and the DB (0700/0600) untouched (observed). No plugin uninstall hook
  exists (cleanup reasons are disable/reset/delete/restart; delete = session delete). Policy:
  keep data on disable/uninstall; README/FAQ document deletion:
  `rm -rf ~/.openclaw/plugins/oc-family-pack` (or $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/plugins/oc-family-pack)
  after uninstall. Reinstall reuses the data but config must be re-entered and the plugin
  re-enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Worker (dist/store-worker.js, resolved via new URL('./store-worker.js', import.meta.url)) creates <stateDir>/plugins/oc-family-pack/ 0700 and oc-family-pack.sqlite 0600, enables WAL, and applies 0001-initial; a second start applies nothing; a write from the service survives Gateway restart, plugin reinstall (--force), and plugins update; only dist/store-worker.js imports node:sqlite (static check) and the worker reports isMainThread=false; manifest declares backupResources include state plugins/oc-family-pack and openclaw backup create --verify reports no opaque-SQLite warning for it; unknown applied migration ids are logged and the store keeps serving; README/FAQ state that uninstall keeps family data and how to delete it.

title: Messaging service and channel selector
description:
A household picks one messaging service OpenClaw already has configured, then the channel on that service that receives family briefs. Discord is one choice, the one this install uses. Telegram, Slack, Signal, iMessage, and any other installed channel plugin are the same kind of choice. The plugin still has no bot token of its own.

Today the family config stores Discord channel ids and every send passes channel "discord". That works for a Discord household and shuts out every other service OpenClaw already runs.
design:
One service per household.

1. Read the Gateway channels object. A service is a configured section (discord, telegram, slack, signal, imessage, or another installed plugin). If only one is configured, it is the choice and setup does not ask. If several are configured, the selector lists them.
2. Family config stores the service id and a destination key for the shared briefs channel. It does not store a second token. Existing channels, summaryChannel, and members[].discordId keep parsing, and they mean the Discord service.
3. The selector is the same choice in two places. openclaw family setup prints the services and the destinations. The Family page lists them when the signed-in operator can ask the host. Picking prints a config patch. It does not write the live Gateway by itself.
4. Delivery calls the host send with that service id. Discord still sends the embed. Every other service sends the same words as text.
5. A person on the selected service matches the roster the way Discord matches discordId today. A sender on any other service stays a guest. Per-person DMs use that person's id on the selected service. discordId remains the Discord id.
6. Out of scope: two services at once, a channel directory of our own, and posting the how-to message.
acceptance_criteria: A Discord-only config still loads and still sends embeds to the summary channel. With two configured services, setup and the page list the services, then the destinations for the chosen one, and the printed patch names that service. A send for a non-Discord service uses that service id and text, and carries no Discord embed. A sender on the selected service resolves to the roster person. npm run check passes. No second bot token, and no live Gateway change.

title: Household access modes in onboarding: solo and LAN (local only)
description: OpenClaw has no built-in per-person login: gateway auth is none|token|password|trusted-proxy (src/config/types.gateway.ts:53) plus the Tailscale identity flag. Onboarding presents three modes and detects which one the Gateway is in: (1) Solo: token/password, every browser is the shared Owner; family uses Discord. (2) LAN household: trusted-proxy behind a self-hosted identity proxy on the trusted LAN, e.g. Caddy forward_auth + Authelia (local family accounts, passkeys; Remote-User header) or Authentik (can federate Discord login, so family signs in with the same Discord account the bot knows). (3) Internet household: Tailscale Serve or Cloudflare Access. Every per-person mode needs HTTPS with a certificate family devices trust, because native plugin pages require secure cookies even on a trusted LAN (docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md:29-31): a real domain with DNS-01 certificates pointing at the LAN address avoids installing a local CA on phones. The plugin guides and checks; it does not deploy proxies. Include a suggested gateway.roles block (parent, kid, guest) and the users.setRole step after first sign-in.
notes:
Operator decision: LAN mode uses simple per-person username/password. Default recipe: Caddy basic_auth with one bcrypt entry per family member (caddy hash-password), header_up X-Forwarded-User {http.auth.user.id} (overwrites any client-supplied value), reverse_proxy to the loopback Gateway; Gateway auth.mode trusted-proxy, trustedProxy.userHeader x-forwarded-user, trustedProxies [127.0.0.1] with allowLoopback only if Caddy is the sole local listener and the Gateway is not directly reachable, allowUsers = the family usernames. Caddy also terminates HTTPS (DNS-01 certificate for a real domain pointed at the LAN address, or Caddy's internal CA if the family is willing to trust it). Authelia stays the upgrade path if the household wants a login page, logout, or passkeys. Onboarding prints the Caddyfile and Gateway config for the entered usernames; the plugin never stores passwords.
Prereq review 2026-09-30: document operator setup per mode. All: Custom plugin UI lab flag (gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins) and HTTPS or loopback for native pages. LAN trusted-proxy: removes the shared gateway token (password fallback remains), needs allowLoopback true and 127.0.0.1 in trustedProxies, exact allowUsers, scopes via deviceAutoApprove/identityScopes; browsers on the Gateway host itself cannot sign in through Caddy. Each login created its own profile. The display name is the basic-auth username. users.setRole, called with the local password fallback, assigned parent and kid.

identityScopes is the grant and the role is the ceiling. Caddy has to overwrite X-Forwarded-User and X-Forwarded-For. The forwarded client address has to be a non-loopback address. allowLoopback is required when Caddy and the Gateway are on the same host, and that same-host loopback sign-in worked.

Question corpus: person location / who's home is the top intent (~19% of human messages; kids ask 'where is Dad'). Needs HA person.* entities, UniFi MACs from the roster, role aliases (Dad/Mom) in the card, fresh pulls (~10 min is stale), and a 'me' default. Promoted to P2 for workshop.
2026-10-04: Nothing in oc-family-pack talks to Home Assistant or UniFi. The only trace is the optional members[].devices list from s5k.3 (label, MAC, source). The page, the tools, and the briefs never read it. Bernie polls a UniFi controller and Home Assistant person/device_tracker entities to answer who is home. That needs installs most households do not have. Do not build it into this plugin. It stays a separate later plugin a household can skip. Dropped from P2 to P4.
